claims.text: In-situ synchrotron XRD with environmental control can simultaneously monitor oxidation kinetics and phase transformations in high-temperature materials.
The proposed method is applicable above 1000°C in a controlled oxidizing atmosphere.
Formation of oxide layers causes changes in the XRD diffraction pattern.
Phase transformations cause changes in the XRD diffraction pattern.
High-temperature oxidation and phase changes alter the material's crystal structure.
Oxidation and phase changes produce distinct shifts or evolution of synchrotron XRD peaks.
Evolution of diffraction peaks enables real-time tracking of oxidation kinetics.
Evolution of diffraction peaks enables real-time tracking of phase stability.
The method will reveal distinct, time-resolved signatures of oxidation processes and phase transformations.
The method will provide insight into the concurrent evolution of oxide layers and phase stability.
Traditional ex-situ methods cannot capture the simultaneous dynamics of phase change and oxidation kinetics.
Temporal resolution, signal noise at extreme temperatures, and overlapping diffraction peaks may limit simultaneous detection.
Current in-situ synchrotron XRD resolution may limit quantification of rapid oxidation events and detection of transient phases.
